correctness.rationale: The uniform-field proof in the lawfully available full Rayudu–Takahashi source was compared at the critical Lemma 6, Lemma 7, Proposition 8, Lemma 9, and Theorems 10–11. For site-dependent h_i>0, the Trotter polynomial's physical variables are y*_{i,m}=e^{-2εh_i}. The source's Lee–Yang zero-free region is the full polydisc |y_{i,m}|<1, not only a common uniform-field line; the cut-at-dead-layer support lemma is field-independent. On |λ|=e^{εh_*} one has |λy*_{i,m}|=e^{εh_*-2εh_i}<=e^{-εh_*}<=e^{-εh_*/2}; hence the source's Borel–Carathéodory bound (with C*=max(n,6βW)) and support order d_k yield |f_{S,ε}(k)|<=128C*/(εh_*)e^{-εh_*d_k}. The Trotter comparison uses only the operator bound Γ=3W+Σh_i (all h_i>0) and [Σh_i Z_i,Z_S]=0, so CT=48(βΓ²+W) and the adaptive ε yield |f_S(t)|<=K e^{-h_*min(t,β-t)/2} with polynomial K(β). The positive spectral representation at β/2 and diagonal-Z_S separation of low energy states prove unique ground and gap≥h_*/4. Independently diagonalized 210 random admissible finite Hamiltonians (n=2,3,4), observing no counterexample; not treated as proof. The bound is finite-volume, requires strictly positive minimum field and claims no optimality.

value.rationale: Uniform gap theorems in quantum many-body models do not automatically control arbitrary nonuniform positive fields. The coordinatewise Lee–Yang contour yields a graph- and coupling-independent gap depending only on the minimum local field, a useful structural robustness theorem. It does not give optimal constant or extend to sign-changing fields.
